why: No major reviewer answers 'best under $300 for camping' head-on, but Yahoo Tech (Rick Broida) runtime-tested the identical ~290Wh unit class under a $250 framing, which is enough to compete with. Everything else is niche spec-comparison sites (Volt & Valley, WattRatings, GearRanking, Outdoor Tech Lab, SolarScout, WattPicks) with affiliate links and unverifiable testing claims, a spec database, a manual, and a generic listicle. A Dealectric page with cart-tested current prices, codes and a direct camping pick could get in, but would be ranked against one tested mainstream article.
